items.title: Critical OpenSSL vulnerability patched in latest release
items.summary: Maintainers urge immediate upgrades; the flaw allows remote attackers to trigger a denial-of-service condition under specific TLS handshakes.

items.title: CISA adds three actively exploited flaws to its KEV catalog
items.summary: Federal agencies must remediate the bugs within three weeks under binding operational direction.

items.title: Researchers detail new phishing kit evading MFA via realtime proxies
items.summary: The kit tunnels victim sessions in real time, defeating most push-based second factors.

items.title: Cloud provider misconfiguration exposed 4M customer records
items.summary: A public storage bucket left names, emails, and partial payment metadata accessible for weeks.

items.title: Linux kernel 6.10 hardens BPF subsystem against privilege escalation
items.summary: New bounds checks close a path that could let unprivileged users escalate to root via crafted eBPF programs.

items.title: Ransomware crew shifts to dataless extortion, leaks in stages
items.summary: Analysts note a move away from encryption toward staged public disclosures to pressure victims.

items.title: New CVE scoring debate: should exploitability weigh more than impact?
items.summary: A long-form argument that current CVSS weighting under-rates wormable but low-impact flaws.

items.title: Patch Tuesday: Microsoft addresses 90 flaws, one wormable RCE
items.summary: Administrators should prioritize the remote code execution bug affecting SMB deployments.
